propositions: A deterministic AST gate must detect six prohibited categories (ambient env read, helper-shim env read, load_config call, literal getattr on os.environ, provider-credential read outside boundary, configurable adapter default) in non-seam modules and report path/symbol/access-kind/owner-seam diagnostics.

The gate must reuse gen_env_registry.py's scan/KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS/matchers as single source, resolve callee and receiver aliases (import/local forms), and fail closed on unresolved/dynamic env reads and shim-shaped callees absent from the helper table.

Owner sets must be derived at runtime from _child_env.owned_secret_names(), a static @register decorator scan of adapters/, and gen_env_registry.scan union with _deprecations, not hand-copied or path-globbed; newly declared env names lacking owners must fail.

Approved seams split into composition roots (*/config.py, _config_sources.py, _child_env.py, LLM adapters) owning categories 1–4, and provider-credential boundaries (src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/ modules) owning category 5 reads.
A legacy-exception registry with exact path+symbol+rationale entries allows introducing the gate without product-code changes, draining to empty in C3.

Synthetic fixtures for all six categories and each aliasing form must fail with expected diagnostics; clean approved-seam fixtures pass; self-tests (bypass, unowned name, path glob, missing rationale) must fail; runs offline with no network/CI dependency.
